import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 3.20

by A. I. Kokorin

Does the class of orderable groups coincide with the smallest axiomatizable class
containing pro-orderable groups? (See 1.35.)

All orders on a group are two-sided invariant here: a *partial order* of a group
$G$ is a partial order $\leq$ on $G$ such that $a \leq b$ implies $ca \leq cb$ and
$ac \leq bc$ for all $a, b, c \in G$. A group is *orderable* if it admits a linear
order of this kind. Following Problem 1.35, a group is *pro-orderable* (an
$O^*$-group) if each of its partial orders can be extended to a linear order.
A class of groups is *axiomatizable* if it is the class of all models of some set
of first-order sentences in the language of groups. The smallest axiomatizable
class containing the pro-orderable groups is the class of models of their
first-order theory.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language

namespace Kourovka.«3.20»

/-- The function symbols of the first-order language of groups: a binary
multiplication, a unary inversion and a constant for the identity. -/
inductive GroupFunc : ℕ → Type
  | mul : GroupFunc 2
  | inv : GroupFunc 1
  | one : GroupFunc 0

/-- The first-order language of groups, with function symbols `*`, `⁻¹` and `1`
and no relation symbols. -/
def groupLanguage : Language where
  Functions := GroupFunc
  Relations _ := Empty

/-- Every group is a structure for the language of groups, with the symbols
interpreted by the group operations. -/
instance (G : Type*) [Group G] : groupLanguage.Structure G where
  funMap {n} f :=
    match n, f with
    | _, .mul => fun x => x 0 * x 1
    | _, .inv => fun x => (x 0)⁻¹
    | _, .one => fun _ => 1
  RelMap r := (r : Empty).elim

/-- A binary relation on a group is bi-invariant if it is preserved by
multiplication on the left and on the right. -/
def IsBiInvariant {G : Type*} [Group G] (r : G → G → Prop) : Prop :=
  Covariant G G (· * ·) r ∧ Covariant G G (Function.swap (· * ·)) r

/-- A group is orderable if it admits a bi-invariant linear order. -/
def IsOrderable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ r : G → G → Prop, IsLinearOrder G r ∧ IsBiInvariant r

/-- A group is pro-orderable (an $O^*$-group) if every bi-invariant partial order
on it can be extended to a bi-invariant linear order. -/
def IsProOrderable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ r : G → G → Prop, IsPartialOrder G r → IsBiInvariant r →
    ∃ s : G → G → Prop, IsLinearOrder G s ∧ IsBiInvariant s ∧ ∀ a b, r a b → s a b

/-- A class `C` of groups is axiomatizable if there is a set `T` of first-order
sentences in the language of groups such that a group belongs to `C` exactly when
it is a model of `T`. -/
def IsAxiomatizable (C : Set GrpCat) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : groupLanguage.Theory, ∀ G : GrpCat, G ∈ C ↔ G ⊨ T

/--
Does the class of orderable groups coincide with the smallest axiomatizable class
containing pro-orderable groups?

The statement says that the class of orderable groups is the least element, under
inclusion, of the family of axiomatizable classes of groups that contain every
pro-orderable group. Every pro-orderable group is orderable and the class of
orderable groups is axiomatizable, so this asks whether every orderable group
satisfies every first-order sentence that holds in all pro-orderable groups.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 6 20]
theorem kourovka.«3.20» : answer(sorry) ↔
    IsLeast {C : Set GrpCat.{0} | IsAxiomatizable C ∧ {G : GrpCat | IsProOrderable G} ⊆ C}
      {G : GrpCat | IsOrderable G} := by
  sorry

/-- Every pro-orderable group is orderable: the trivial partial order extends to
a bi-invariant linear order. -/
@[category API, AMS 6 20]
theorem IsProOrderable.isOrderable {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsProOrderable G) :
    IsOrderable G := by
  obtain ⟨s, hs, hs', -⟩ := h (· = ·)
    { refl := fun _ => rfl, trans := fun _ _ _ => Eq.trans, antisymm := fun _ _ h _ => h }
    ⟨fun _ _ _ h => congrArg _ h, fun _ _ _ h => congrArg (· * _) h⟩
  exact ⟨s, hs, hs'⟩

@[category test, AMS 6 20]
theorem isOrderable_multiplicative_int : IsOrderable (Multiplicative ℤ) :=
  ⟨(· ≤ ·), inferInstance, fun _ _ _ h => mul_le_mul_right h _,
    fun _ _ _ h => mul_le_mul_left h _⟩

/-- The sentence $\forall x\, \forall y,\ x y = y x$ of the language of groups. -/
def commSentence : groupLanguage.Sentence :=
  ∀' ∀' (Functions.apply₂ (GroupFunc.mul : groupLanguage.Functions 2) (&0) (&1) ='
    Functions.apply₂ (GroupFunc.mul : groupLanguage.Functions 2) (&1) (&0))

@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem multiplicative_int_models_commSentence : Multiplicative ℤ ⊨ commSentence := by
  simp only [commSentence, Sentence.Realize, Formula.Realize, BoundedFormula.realize_all,
    BoundedFormula.realize_bdEqual, Term.realize_functions_apply₂]
  intro x y
  exact mul_comm x y

@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem not_perm_models_commSentence : ¬ Equiv.Perm (Fin 3) ⊨ commSentence := by
  simp only [commSentence, Sentence.Realize, Formula.Realize, BoundedFormula.realize_all,
    BoundedFormula.realize_bdEqual, Term.realize_functions_apply₂]
  intro h
  have := congrArg (· 0) (h (Equiv.swap 0 1) (Equiv.swap 1 2))
  exact absurd this (by decide)

end Kourovka.«3.20»

pro-orderable groups? Here an orderable group has a bi-invariant linear order, and a pro-orderable
(or O*-group) is a group in which every bi-invariant partial order extends to a bi-invariant linear

open FirstOrder

/-- The function symbols for the first-order language of groups. -/
inductive groupFunc : ℕ → Type
  | mul : groupFunc 2
  | inv : groupFunc 1
  | one : groupFunc 0
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- The first-order language of groups, with multiplication, inverse, and identity symbols. -/
def groupLanguage : Language where
  Functions := groupFunc
  Relations := fun _ => Empty

/-- The canonical interpretation of the first-order group language on a group. -/
def groupStructure (G : Type) [Group G] : groupLanguage.Structure G where
  funMap := fun {n} f =>
    match n, f with
    | _, .mul => fun x => x 0 * x 1
    | _, .inv => fun x => (x 0)⁻¹
    | _, .one => fun _ => 1
  RelMap := fun {_} r => r.elim

/-- A group satisfies a sentence when the sentence holds in its canonical first-order group
structure. -/
def SatisfiesGroupSentence (G : Type) [Group G] (φ : groupLanguage.Sentence) : Prop :=
  @Language.Sentence.Realize groupLanguage G (groupStructure G) φ

/-- A relation on a group is bi-invariant if left and right multiplication preserve and reflect
it. -/
def IsBiInvariant {G : Type*} [Group G] (r : G → G → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ a b c, (r a b ↔ r (c * a) (c * b)) ∧ (r a b ↔ r (a * c) (b * c))

/-- A group partial order is a bi-invariant partial order on the underlying type. -/
def IsGroupPartialOrder (G : Type*) [Group G] (r : G → G → Prop) : Prop :=
  IsPartialOrder G r ∧ IsBiInvariant r

/-- A group linear order is a bi-invariant linear order on the underlying type. -/
def IsGroupLinearOrder (G : Type*) [Group G] (r : G → G → Prop) : Prop :=
  IsLinearOrder G r ∧ IsBiInvariant r

/-- A group is orderable if it admits a bi-invariant linear order. -/
def IsOrderable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ r : G → G → Prop, IsGroupLinearOrder G r

/-- A group is pro-orderable (an O*-group) if each of its bi-invariant partial orders extends to a
bi-invariant linear order. -/
def IsProOrderable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ r : G → G → Prop, IsGroupPartialOrder G r →
    ∃ s : G → G → Prop, IsGroupLinearOrder G s ∧ ∀ ⦃a b⦄, r a b → s a b

/-- The first-order theory consisting of the group-language sentences true in every pro-orderable
group. -/
def proOrderableTheory : groupLanguage.Theory :=
  {φ | ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsProOrderable G → SatisfiesGroupSentence G φ}

/-- A group is a model of the common first-order theory of the pro-orderable groups. -/
def ModelsProOrderableTheory (G : Type) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ φ ∈ proOrderableTheory, SatisfiesGroupSentence G φ

/--
Does the class of orderable groups coincide with the smallest first-order axiomatizable class
containing the pro-orderable groups? Equivalently, does every group admitting a bi-invariant linear
order satisfy every first-order group sentence that holds in every group whose bi-invariant partial
orders all extend to bi-invariant linear orders?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«3.20» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsOrderable G → ModelsProOrderableTheory G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«3.20»

  MulLeftMono G ∧ MulRightMono G

/-- A group is *orderable* if it admits a two-sided invariant linear order. -/
def IsOrderable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=

order `p` on `G` can be extended to a two-sided invariant linear order `l` on `G`, i.e.

def IsProOrderable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=

open FirstOrder Language

namespace Kourovka.«3.20»

/-- A binary relation `le` on a group `G` is *two-sided invariant* if `le a b` implies
`le (x * a * y) (x * b * y)` for all `x y : G`, i.e. $a \le b$ implies $x a y \le x b y$. -/
def IsBiInvariant {G : Type*} [Group G] (le : G → G → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ a b x y : G, le a b → le (x * a * y) (x * b * y)

/-- A group is *orderable* if it admits a linear order that is invariant under multiplication on
both sides. -/
def IsOrderable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ l : LinearOrder G, IsBiInvariant l.le

/-- A group is *pro-orderable* (an $O^*$-group) if every partial order on it that is invariant
under multiplication on both sides can be extended to a linear order that is invariant under
multiplication on both sides. -/
def IsProOrderable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ p : PartialOrder G, IsBiInvariant p.le →
    ∃ l : LinearOrder G, IsBiInvariant l.le ∧ ∀ a b : G, p.le a b → l.le a b

/-- Every pro-orderable group is orderable: extend the trivial partial order. -/
@[category API, AMS 6 20]
theorem IsProOrderable.isOrderable {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsProOrderable G) :
    IsOrderable G := by
  obtain ⟨l, hl, -⟩ := h
    { le := (· = ·)
      le_refl := fun _ => rfl
      le_trans := fun _ _ _ => Eq.trans
      le_antisymm := fun _ _ h _ => h }
    (fun _ _ _ _ h => by rw [h]; exact rfl)
  exact ⟨l, hl⟩

/-- The function symbols of the first-order language of groups: a binary multiplication, a unary
inversion and a constant for the identity. -/
inductive GroupFunc : ℕ → Type
  | mul : GroupFunc 2
  | inv : GroupFunc 1
  | one : GroupFunc 0

symbols. -/
def groupLanguage : Language where
  Functions := GroupFunc
  Relations _ := Empty

/-- A group `G` as a structure for the language of groups, interpreting the function symbols by
the group operations. -/

  funMap {n} f :=
    match n, f with
    | _, .mul => fun x => x 0 * x 1
    | _, .inv => fun x => (x 0)⁻¹
    | _, .one => fun _ => 1
  RelMap r := Empty.elim r

of groups that hold in every pro-orderable group. The class of groups satisfying this theory is
